dossier.public_summary: The dip changes from undetected to several percent between TESS sectors and individual transits, varying by a factor of 10. On this rapidly spotted M dwarf the 15-day signal repeats about three times the star's 4.5-day spin with strong spot modulation. This, plus too few flat-bottomed transits and no on-target centroid, is best explained by stellar variability/blend rather than a 4.1 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Individual transit depths wildly inconsistent: 24711 ppm in sector 66 rejected as outlier sigma 5.9, chi2 60.0 over dof 3, share_of_top_3 0.997, p_consistent 5.83e-13, indicating not a steady planet transit.
Depth changes 202.2% across sectors, per_sector 1378-24711 ppm. sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source with QLP p_constant 6.09e-09, so variation is real not calibration.

15-d signal is ~3.3x the stellar rotation period (4.54 d, amplitude 21716 ppm in sector 39), phase_curve amplitude 1378 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.1729, consistent with active M-dwarf spot variability systematics rather than a flat-bottomed planet.

No sector with a clear difference image; cannot localize dip to target, with neighbours plausible_within_1px 2 and could_cause 179. Combined with depth variability and xgboost planet_rank 0.05, other explanations best.
